qualifying_findings.title: Spring AI 2.0.1 fixes AI framework vulnerabilities including prompt-injection tool dispatch
qualifying_findings.summary: Spring AI 2.0.1 lists seven fixed CVEs. The most AI-agent-specific advisory, CVE-2026-59318, says Spring AI advertised per-request tool lists to the model but did not fully enforce them during dispatch, allowing an unavailable tool to be invoked under some conditions and potentially leading to privilege escalation. Related Spring AI advisories cover semantic-cache cross-context leakage and Redis chat-memory query injection that can expose messages across conversations.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary vendor release and security advisories
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Spring AI 2.0.0, 1.1.0-1.1.8, and 1.0.0-1.0.9 for CVE-2026-59318; Spring AI 2.0.0 for CVE-2026-59308 and CVE-2026-59319; fixed in 2.0.1 OSS with enterprise support fixes for older lines where listed.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The tool-dispatch advisory is a concrete example of prompt-level authorization boundaries failing unless the runtime enforces least privilege. The cache and chat-memory advisories map to AI data-isolation and conversation-boundary controls.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Spring AI as a framework/product belongs upstream if broad framework coverage is needed.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General Spring AI development practices and release mechanics belong upstream in ai-dev-wiki.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Keep the prompt-injection tool-dispatch bypass, AI cache isolation, chat-memory exposure, affected versions, and patch guidance.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence: primary Spring pages expose dates, affected versions, mitigations, and CVE IDs inside the cutoff window.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, decide whether the local security wiki needs a Spring AI vulnerability leaf or whether these fit an existing AI framework supply-chain/runtime-security page.
Check NVD/GitHub advisory records later for CVSS and CWE normalization if durable synthesis needs vulnerability database metadata.

qualifying_findings.title: Adversa discloses Cryptographic Context Injection against Grok and Gemini
qualifying_findings.summary: Adversa described Cryptographic Context Injection, where encrypted instructions are decrypted inside a model or agent code-execution runtime and then treated as trusted runtime output. The report says a Grok browsing scenario could exfiltrate private session context and chat history through an outbound navigation tool without user confirmation, and a Gemini Deep Thinking scenario could bypass safety filtering by returning prohibited output as ciphertext.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary security research with reputable security press corroboration
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: xAI Grok web chat agentic browsing framework; Google Gemini public chat interface in Deep Thinking mode. Adversa says Grok remained reproducible as of August 19, 2026; Gemini success had fallen but was not fully closed.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The finding shifts prompt-injection defense from text filtering to provenance, runtime-output trust, tool egress gating, and agent harness controls, especially for agents with code execution, browsing, credentials, or write authority.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Grok, Gemini, xAI, Google, and general model/product background are upstream-owned.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General agent harness design practice is upstream-owned unless framed as a security control.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Keep the attack pattern, disclosure state, zero-click exfiltration boundary, and harness mitigation implications.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence on public disclosure timing and technical claims as reported by Adversa; vendor remediation status is based on researcher statements and should be rechecked during ingest.
follow_up_actions: Track whether xAI or Google publish a formal response or mitigation.
Map the attack to existing prompt-injection, tool-output provenance, and agent egress-control pages if present.

qualifying_findings.title: US agencies warn of AI-generated exploit scripts targeting Siemens S7 PLCs
qualifying_findings.summary: NSA, CISA, FBI, DOE, and EPA issued advisory AA26-231A warning that threat actors are using open-source industrial automation libraries such as snap7.dll and python-snap7 with AI-assisted scripting to create tools that mimic legitimate OT monitoring software and provide read/write access to Siemens S7 PLC memory, configuration data, and ladder logic via S7comm. The activity targets exposed or poorly segmented devices in critical manufacturing, energy, water and wastewater, chemical, food and agriculture, and commercial facilities.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary government advisory identified, with in-window secondary reporting used for exact window qualification
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Siemens S7-200, S7-300, S7-400, S7-1200, and S7-1500 product lines; especially internet-exposed or weakly segmented PLCs using S7comm and weak/default credentials.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: This is an operational public example of AI lowering the expertise and time needed to build exploitation scripts for critical infrastructure, making AI-enabled offensive capability and defensive monitoring a local AI-security concern.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Siemens and broad OT/PLC background are not local AI-security entity pages unless needed as context.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General AI-assisted code generation practice is upstream-owned.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Keep the AI-generated exploit-script capability, affected OT boundary, mitigation controls, and critical-infrastructure risk implications.

qualifying_findings.title: OpenAI previews ZDR-compatible Private Safety Processing
qualifying_findings.summary: OpenAI previewed Private Safety Processing for eligible Zero Data Retention deployments. The design aims to analyze related interactions for misuse patterns while keeping customer prompts and responses unavailable to OpenAI personnel, with customer-controlled infrastructure or future customer-controlled encryption keys and only limited safety signals returned to OpenAI.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary product security/privacy control page with in-window secondary reporting for visible date
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: OpenAI API frontier-model deployments for eligible ZDR customers; early customer testing, planned rollout and technical white paper in September 2026.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: This is a concrete control change at the tension point between agentic misuse monitoring and enterprise data confidentiality. It belongs in AI safety monitoring, privacy, audit evidence, and customer-controlled content boundary tracking.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: OpenAI and broad API platform/product coverage are upstream-owned.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General API integration practice is upstream-owned.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Keep the ZDR-compatible misuse detection control, privacy boundary, customer-controlled key model, and monitoring/audit implications.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: Medium confidence for in-window qualification because the OpenAI page exposes only a year in fetched content; Help Net Security provides the August 20 visible date and links to the OpenAI page.
follow_up_actions: Recheck OpenAI for a technical white paper in September 2026.

qualifying_findings.title: AWS publishes downstream authorization pattern for Bedrock AgentCore agents
qualifying_findings.summary: AWS described a pattern for propagating user authorization context through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore so downstream systems, not the agent, enforce access decisions. The example uses identity-provider claims, Bedrock AgentCore Runtime authorization, session-tagged credentials, metadata filtering for knowledge bases, and on-behalf-of token exchange for Salesforce so prompt injection or agent bugs cannot grant access beyond the requesting user.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary cloud-provider security architecture guidance with in-window secondary reporting
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime and Identity patterns for agents accessing DynamoDB, Bedrock Knowledge Bases, Salesforce, and similar data sources.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The item gives a concrete least-privilege architecture for delegated AI agents, separating orchestration from authorization and limiting credential exposure even when prompt manipulation succeeds.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: AWS, Bedrock, and AgentCore broad product coverage are upstream-owned.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General agent implementation patterns are upstream-owned when not security-specific.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Keep the user-bound credential propagation, downstream authorization, prompt-injection-resistant least privilege, and audit/control implications.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: Medium confidence for exact-window qualification because the primary AWS post is date-only August 19, which is boundary-only for this run; the in-window Help Net Security coverage supplies the August 20 date.

qualifying_findings.title: Darktrace reports fake Gemini installer delivering Vidar via Google Colab lure
qualifying_findings.summary: Darktrace reported an EMEA customer incident in which a malicious executable named Download_Google_Gemini_For_Windows.exe masqueraded as a Google Gemini installer. The lure used a Google Colab page and a secondary Windows Software Hub site to deliver a newer Go-compiled Vidar infostealer variant that contacted Telegram-based infrastructure and a C2 endpoint, with observed credential-theft indicators before containment.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary incident research with in-window secondary reporting
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Fake Google Gemini software acquisition workflow; Google Colab-hosted lure; Vidar infostealer; observed July 2026 with Colab page active at July 15 review.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: This is a concrete AI-themed social-engineering and brand-impersonation incident where enterprise AI adoption interest becomes the lure for credential theft, relevant to AI product trust, identity, and user workflow controls.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Gemini and Google Colab broad product pages are upstream-owned.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General developer use of Colab belongs upstream if needed.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Keep the AI-themed lure, trusted-platform abuse, malware delivery path, credential-theft implication, and containment lessons.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: Medium confidence for exact-window qualification because the primary Darktrace date is date-only August 19 and therefore boundary-only, but Help Net Security reported the incident on August 20.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, avoid implying the legitimate Gemini product was compromised.
